one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled/expected events fall inside the window. (1) Q3 2026 results, expected ~Oct 28 (consensus EPS ~$0.36 vs Q2 adjusted $0.28): management guided to a stronger H2 on grade sequencing, Copper Mountain SAG repair completed (~1 month outage from late June) and Constancia pebble crushers from Q3, and copper averaged ~$6.5/lb (LME ~$14.4-14.7k/t in early September) with gold ~$4,100/oz, so the print should be good, but much of this is visible to the market already. (2) Copper World DFS/FID, which management said would come 'early Q4' with capex explicitly flagged as higher than the 2023 PFS ($1.3B Phase 1); a capex-inflation headline could be a modest negative even as sanction itself de-risks the story. Net: a slight upward tilt in the median (~$26.35 vs $26.18) and a monthly sigma of ~17.5% (63% annual / 3.5, close to the stock's usual), i.e. near-symmetric; the dominant driver over a month remains copper/gold price moves, on which I take no view.

fair_value.method: Blend of 2027E EV/EBITDA (6.5x on ~$1.75B EBITDA -> ~$25.8), 2027E P/E (15x on ~$1.75 EPS -> ~$26.3) and P/NAV (1.15x on a ~$23.4/sh NAV at long-term $4.75/lb Cu and $3,000/oz Au -> ~$27), with a small upward tilt because spot metals (~$6.5 Cu, ~$4,100 Au) are well above the NAV deck; rounded to $27.

155kt x 2,204.6 x $5.75 = $1.96B Cu + 240koz x $3,700 = $0.89B Au + ~$0.2B zinc/silver/moly by-products.

Mid-tier copper producers typically trade ~5.5-8x forward EBITDA; 6.5x reflects a net-cash balance sheet (net debt/EBITDA -0.1x) and a large US growth pipeline offset by heavy upcoming Copper World capex. Current EV ~$11.55B is ~6.6x my 2027E.
June 30, 2026: cash $890.9M (incl. $334.5M restricted to Copper World), long-term debt $860.2M.
444,144,760 after issuing 46.8M shares for Arizona Sonoran on June 24, 2026.

bear.story: Copper retreats toward $4.5/lb and gold toward $3,200 as the cycle cools; Copper World DFS capex comes in well above $2B and FID slips or requires heavy funding; Copper Mountain keeps missing throughput; Peru political/social disruption at Constancia. EBITDA ~$1.1B, multiple compresses to ~5.5x.

base.story: 2027 guidance delivered (~150-160kt Cu, ~240koz Au) at Cu ~$5.5-6/lb; Copper World sanctioned late 2026 with Mitsubishi's $180M paid by mid-2027; balance sheet stays near net cash; stock re-rates modestly on volume growth.

bull.story: Copper deficit narrative holds with Cu $7+/lb and gold >$4,000; 2027 production at top of 140-184kt range; Copper World built on budget with project finance; Cactus/Mason studies show a credible path to 500kt; NTM EBITDA ~$2.6B at 7x.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$16 (about -39%, roughly the bear case and near the lower end of the 52-week range) the market would be pricing either a copper price collapse below ~$4.5/lb, a Copper World capex/funding shock that forces equity issuance, or a major operating failure (Constancia disruption in Peru, Copper Mountain not reaching 50ktpd), rather than ordinary 60%-vol noise; at that level EV would be ~5x even a haircut-deck 2027 EBITDA.

reasoning: Hudbay Minerals is now a ~$11.6B market-cap (444.1M shares post Arizona Sonoran deal) copper-gold producer with a net-cash balance sheet ($80.5M net cash at Q2, net debt/EBITDA -0.1x), H1 2026 adjusted EBITDA $743M and FCF $205M, improved 2026 cash cost guidance (-$0.45 to -$0.25/lb), and a three-year outlook pointing to ~24% higher copper in 2027 (140-184kt). Spot metals are very strong (Cu ~$6.5/lb, Au ~$4,100). My three methods (EV/EBITDA 6.5x on $1.75B 2027E, P/E 15x on $1.75, P/NAV 1.15x) cluster at $26-27, i.e. the stock is roughly fairly priced on haircut prices and cheap at spot; the upside is mostly a metals-price call plus Copper World/Cactus/Mason option value, and the downside is a metals reversal or a capex shock at Copper World (management already flagged capex above the 2023 PFS). Scenario mix (bear $15/25%, base $28/50%, bull $40/25%) gives a mean ~$27.75. For the ladder I used a lognormal with median $26.8 (slight drift for fair value + ~0.04% dividend + metals-cycle momentum) and sigma 0.48, below the 63% realized vol because the past year included a +77% re-rating and the net-cash balance sheet limits distress risk, but still well above a large-cap's 25-35%; I fattened the far-left tail slightly for mining-specific event risk. Research was limited: Twelve Data analyst/estimate endpoints and Alpha Vantage were unavailable (plan/rate limits), direct SEC curl was blocked so filings were read via WebFetch summaries, and the analyst target data found was stale and not used numerically.
